en.hero.eyebrow: Paired agent benchmark · GreptimeDB Semantic Graph
en.hero.lede: Same models, same incidents, three observability interfaces: Prometheus with Loki and Tempo, GreptimeDB, and GreptimeDB with its Semantic Graph. The measurement covers three outcomes: how often the root cause was located, the investigation work a correct diagnosis took, and what the runs cost.
en.hero.title: Does the observability interface behind the agent change root cause analysis?
en.interface.lede: Both endpoints specified for this comparison measure work, not accuracy: the steps taken to reach a correct diagnosis, and the tokens the model had to read.
en.interface.rows_note: Rows returned cannot be compared here. A Prometheus sample, a Loki entry and a Tempo trace are not the same unit as a GreptimeDB row, so rows returned reports N/A against the three-backend bundle instead of zero.
en.interface.title: Finding 1 — GreptimeDB against three backends
en.method.evidence_note: The deterministic verifier reads SQL. It is published as a separate audit and does not decide headline eligibility.
en.method.rejection_note: The verifier runs its mechanism check over every citation, including ones submitted as exclusion or downstream-impact evidence that never claimed to prove the mechanism. Only the first column describes an attempt that fell short; the second only shows how wide the check reaches. A code in either column does not by itself mean a claim failed, because another citation may already ground it.
en.method.title: Method and limits
en.metric.correct_completion_tool_calls.not: tool calls in a run that ended in a correct diagnosis
en.metric.provider_visible_input_tokens: Tokens the model had to read
en.metric.rows_returned.note: rows returned by the queries the agent ran
en.models.score_note: A descriptive index computed after the measurement, out of {max} points split {split} between location, root cause and executed evidence. Scores are normalised to 100 over each model's {runs} end-to-end runs, with failed runs left in the denominator. It is not a pre-specified endpoint and carries no significance test.
en.models.title: How the models differed
en.overview.evidence_note: Two comparison families were specified and frozen in the protocol before any run, together with their metrics and the Holm family size. Everything else on this page is descriptive. "Pre-specified" here means frozen in a hashed protocol fixture in this repository; there is no public third-party registration. An endpoint counts only if it survives Holm correction within its family at the {alpha} level. Where a case median points is recorded as a direction and nothing more; a direction is not a weaker kind of result.
en.overview.setup_lede: Every model investigates every incident {total} times: {repetitions} runs through each of the {interfaces} interfaces. The telemetry, the incident, the prompt and the tool budget are identical every time. Only the interface changes.
en.overview.title: What we found

en.question.model_ranking: How do the models differ at RCA under each interface?
en.question.semantic_layer: Does the complete GreptimeDB Semantic Graph interface reduce RCA investigation work while preserving diagnosis and evidence validity?
en.question.storage_shape: How does the GreptimeDB all-in-one agent-facing interface compare with a Prometheus, Loki and Tempo native interface bundle on the same incidents? The two differ in store, query languages and tool surface together, so this is an interface-bundle comparison, not an isolated storage effect.
en.relative.lede: Each bar is the median case: the difference in what that interface used against the other on the same incident, counting only cases where both diagnosed correctly.
en.relative.note: median across eligible cases; descriptive, not a pre-specified endpoint
en.resources.lede: Input counts every token the provider charged for reading. Reasoning is part of output, not an addition to it.
en.resources.title: Tokens, cost, and reliability
en.retrieval.discovery.body: The model receives an incident window and no schema. It has to establish which table holds the relevant measurement and what the column is called before it can issue a query. Through GreptimeDB alone that means listing tables, describing them, and running trial queries. Through the Semantic Graph it can query which signal carries a given meaning.
en.retrieval.discovery.title: Discovery: find the signal in an unfamiliar schema
en.retrieval.graph.body: Starting from one service known to be misbehaving, the model has to name its direct dependencies. Through GreptimeDB alone that means reconstructing call relationships from trace spans. Through the Semantic Graph those relationships are already stored and can be queried directly.
en.retrieval.graph.title: Graph retrieval: find what a failing service depends on
en.retrieval.interpretation: A reduction on one step of an investigation does not necessarily reach the total, and this measurement does not isolate which step absorbed it.
en.retrieval.lede: Before a model can reason about a failure it has to locate the data: which table holds the signal, and which service calls which. These two tasks measure that step on its own. Both stop at the first query that returns the evidence, so they measure the cost of locating data, not the cost of diagnosing it.
en.retrieval.metric_note: Rows and calls are counted up to the query that returns the evidence, not across a whole investigation, so they do not compare with the end-to-end metrics.
en.retrieval.title: Retrieval cost fell. End-to-end cost did not.
en.semantic.lede: Both interfaces read the same telemetry from the same GreptimeDB instance. The Semantic Graph is the only difference. The endpoints specified for it are the steps taken to reach a correct diagnosis and the rows the queries returned.
en.semantic.reversal_lede: Correct diagnoses under each interface, grouped by the level the fault sat at.
en.semantic.title: Finding 2 — what the GreptimeDB Semantic Graph changed
en.strip.lede: Each dot is one incident that both interfaces diagnosed correctly. Its position shows what that same correct answer cost under each interface.
en.strip.title: Every eligible case, one point

zh.retrieval.discovery.body: 模型拿到一个故障时间窗，没有 schema。它必须先确定相关测量值所在的表和字段名称，才能发起查询。只用 GreptimeDB 需要列出表、describe、试探性查询；加上语义层可以直接查询哪个信号表示指定含义。
zh.retrieval.discovery.title: Discovery：在陌生 schema 里找到信号
zh.retrieval.graph.body: 从一个已知异常的服务出发，模型需要给出它的直接依赖。只用 GreptimeDB 需要从 trace span 还原调用关系；加上语义层，这些关系已经存储，可直接查询。
zh.retrieval.graph.title: Graph retrieval：找到故障服务依赖了谁
zh.retrieval.interpretation: 调查中某一步的开销下降，不必然反映在总量上；本次测量也没有区分是哪一步吸收了它。
zh.retrieval.lede: 模型推理故障之前，必须先定位数据：信号存放在哪张表，哪个服务调用哪个服务。这两个任务单独测量这一步，都算到第一条返回证据的查询为止，因此衡量的是定位数据的成本，不是诊断的成本。
zh.retrieval.metric_note: Rows 和 calls 只统计到返回证据的那条查询为止，不覆盖整个调查过程，因此不能与端到端指标比较。
zh.retrieval.title: 检索成本下降，端到端调查没有
zh.semantic.lede: 两种接口从同一个 GreptimeDB 实例读同一批遥测数据，唯一的差别是语义层。为它指定的端点是得出正确诊断所用的步数，以及查询返回的行数。
